historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 3yr CAGR (19.1%, FY2022->FY2025) is driven almost entirely by almond PRICE recovery (achieved price +32.4% in FY2025 alone) and the FY2023 trough base, not durable volume/capacity growth -- it diverges sharply from the 10yr revenue CAGR (5.9%) and the 10yr equity CAGR (6.2%). EPS and FCF CAGRs are not meaningful across this history: EPS went from $0.829 (FY2015) through a NEGATIVE base (FY2023: -$0.948, FY2024: ~$0.007) to $0.224 (FY2025), and reported FCF was negative in 6 of the last 10 annual periods (FY2017-18, FY2020-21-22-23) on a business undergoing an orchard/processing capex supercycle followed by a price-driven trough. The equity 10yr CAGR (6.2%) is used as the base-case anchor as the most conservative, least cycle-distorted series, though it is itself suppressed by the FY2023 $114.7m loss and subsequent dilutive equity raises (FY2024 $58.9m, FY2025 $17.4m).

scenario_narratives.base: SHV settles into a normal mid-cycle year on an EBITDA basis, but the true owner-FCF margin normalizes to a thin ~4% once the substantial lease cost and PP&E capex of this lease-heavy commodity processor are deducted -- modest volume/mix-driven growth, no repeat of the FY2025 one-off working-capital release, and cash tax ramping up as carried-forward losses are exhausted.
scenario_narratives.bull: The structural Californian-acreage-decline thesis plays out, the 2030 plan (65,000MT, value-add growth, external grower volumes) executes close to management's targets, and margins expand toward 23.5% EBITDA / ~8% owner FCF on processing scale and cost savings.
scenario_narratives.bear: A FY2023-style shock repeats -- adverse almond price move, weak/wet crop, China demand or trade-policy deterioration, and CEO-transition execution risk on the capital-intensive 2030 targets -- pushing margins back toward the historical trough band with a modestly negative owner-FCF trough in years 1-3.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Select Harvests is valued as a mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF. The headline FY2025 recovery (Underlying EBITDA margin 19.2%, NPAT $31.8m) is real and is used to anchor the base-case EBITDA margin, but the reported owner FCF of $71.2m is NOT taken at face value -- roughly a third of it is a one-off working-capital release from a smaller crop that will not repeat, and once the company's substantial lease cost (it leases a large share of its orchard land) is fully expensed rather than left inside IFRS-16 OCF, the underlying owner-FCF margin of this business is a structurally thin ~4-5% at mid-cycle. Combined with a price-taking commodity model (Californian supply sets the global almond price, ~75-80% of world volume) and heavy China customer concentration, the bear case is materially overweighted (30%) to reflect the demonstrated downside (FY2023 near-loss) and current transition risks (new CEO, capital-intensive 2030 targets).
key_risks_to_valuation: Global almond price volatility (set by Californian supply, ~75-80% of world volume) is the single largest driver of profitability and is outside management's control
Crop yield/weather variability -- FY2025 crop fell 15.7% YoY and NSW orchards remain in multi-year recovery from prior wet seasons
China customer concentration (~60-65% of export sales) exposes SHV to Chinese demand cycles, currency and trade-policy/tariff risk
CEO transition (David Surveyor, credited with the FY23-25 turnaround, departed mid-2026) creates execution risk on the ambitious, capital-intensive 2030 targets (65,000MT capacity, $700m revenue)

IAS 41 biological-asset fair-value accounting introduces large non-cash earnings swings (e.g. -$74.5m FY2023, +$58.8m FY2025) that complicate year-on-year comparability and could mislead a reader who anchors on statutory NPAT rather than the owner-FCF build used here

FY2025's reported owner FCF ($71.2m) embeds a one-off ~$23.7m working-capital release (from a 15.7% smaller crop) that will not repeat and reverses as the crop and revenue grow again -- a reader anchoring on that $71.2m figure will overstate sustainable cash generation by roughly a third
Seasonal working-capital debt swings (net debt ranges from ~$79m at FY2025 year-end to ~$183m mid-cycle per H1 FY2026 disclosure) mean a poor crop or price year compounds with balance-sheet strain

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3.45-5.21 AUD
data_sources.financials: research/SHV.AX/Reports/SHV.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics export) and research/SHV.AX/Extracted/SHV.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt (FY2025 Annual Report, restated FY2024 comparatives per note 1.3)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report note 6.3 'Employee performance rights' equity movement ($816k FY2025, $272k FY2024); SBC is immaterial (~0.2% of revenue) in this AUD-filed agribusiness
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD risk-free rate (~4.2% AU 10yr) + ERP ~5.5% + a small cyclical/commodity-agribusiness premium, giving 9.5% -- broadly in line with the house's non-US industrial reference (~9%) but a touch higher for global-commodity price-taker risk and China customer concentration. Risk is expressed primarily through the scenario dispersion (bear/bull driver paths) rather than stacked further onto WACC, per the 'charge risk once' rule; the same 9.5% is used across all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Full lease payment (principal $23.628m FY2025 financing outflow + interest $10.963m already inside operating cash flow) is deducted inside the owner-FCF build; lease liabilities ($215.887m gross, current+non-current) are EXCLUDED from net_debt. This matches the company's own disclosed 'Net Debt' KPI (FY2025 $79.068m = borrowings $80.440m less cash $1.372m, i.e. debt-only, no lease liabilities), so the model's net-debt bridge is internally consistent with management's own gearing convention. Reported OCF already nets lease INTEREST (an operating cash flow line); only lease PRINCIPAL needed an additional deduction to reach last_fcf: (OCF $118.642m - capex $22.860m) - lease principal $23.628m - SBC $0.816m - interest income $0.136m = $71.202m. IMPORTANT CALIBRATION NOTE: that $71.202m includes a one-off $23.7m FAVOURABLE working-capital release (receivables/inventory unwound because FY2025 crop volume fell 15.7% YoY) plus ~$5.9m of gain-on-asset-sale and other non-cash reconciling items that sit between EBITDA and OCF. Rebuilding FY2025 bottom-up from reported Underlying EBITDA ($76.625m) through SBC/lease/D&A(PPE-only, $28.041m)/tax/capex, EXCLUDING that one-off working-capital release, gives a normalized owner-FCF margin of ~4.6% ($18.4m before any wc swing on $398.258m revenue) -- this normalized figure, not the swing-inflated $71.2m, is what the projection's Year-1 driver path is calibrated to reproduce. last_fcf/reported_fcf are still reported on the full actual (swing-inclusive) basis for auditability.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- Select Harvests has no reported minority interests; all subsidiaries wholly owned.
inputs.notes: Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md as a non-US, cyclical operating company (agricultural commodity grower/processor) -> owner-FCF DCF (references/owner-fcf.md) + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (leases, cyclical risk-charge-once). No prior DCF/Drivers file exists for SHV.AX; this is a FRESH BUILD. FY2024 comparatives used throughout are the RESTATED figures from the FY2025 Annual Report (net income $0.898m not $1.500m; OCF $9.549m not $21.349m) per note 1.3 Comparative Information. Mid-cycle normalization is central to this build: FY2023 was a near-loss year dominated by a $74.5m adverse biological-asset fair-value swing and $30.1m of impairments (almond price trough); FY2025's headline recovery (Underlying EBITDA margin 19.2%, NPAT $31.8m) is treated as a return to a NORMAL mid-cycle year on an EBITDA basis, but its owner-FCF conversion is NOT extrapolated at face value, because ~$23.7m of the $71.2m reported owner FCF is a one-off working-capital release from a smaller crop, not a repeatable tailwind (see lease_treatment note above for the full reconciliation). Base-case revenue growth (6% tapering to 3%) reflects volume/capacity growth (external grower tonnes, Project Optimus processing expansion, value-added mix), not a repeat of the FY2025 price windfall (+32.4% achieved price). EBITDA margin is held near FY2025's 19.2%, the middle of the FY2020-22 non-distressed historical band (17-25%), improving only gradually. Once the substantial lease cost (~8.5% of revenue -- SHV leases a large share of its orchard land) and PP&E D&A (~7%) are deducted from that EBITDA margin, the resulting owner-FCF margin normalizes to ~4% in the base case, matching the ~4.6% figure derived directly from FY2025 actuals ex the one-off working-capital release -- this is a genuine structural feature of a lease-heavy, capital-intensive commodity processor, not a modelling error. Capex is set at FY2024-25's post-expansion run-rate (~6-7% of revenue) rather than the FY2020-22 supercycle rate (~14-15%), with a modest step-up in years 2-4 for 2030-target capacity growth. Cash tax rate is ramped from a low starting point (FY2020-25 cash tax was zero or negative on carried-forward losses; FY2025 Annual Report note 5.1 states the Group 'is expected to generate taxable income from 2026 onwards' and the losses carry forward indefinitely) up to the 30% AU statutory rate by year 5 -- NOT perpetuating the recent zero-tax years. Working capital capture is NEGATIVE (wc_capture -8% base): this is an inventory/receivables-heavy grower-processor (crop financed through the growing season, seasonal debt swings of ~$100m+ per the Analysis JSON), so revenue growth consumes cash on a normalized basis -- the magnitude is set below the extreme FY2025 actual swing (which was a one-off unwind, not the steady-state direction) but still the opposite sign from a subscription/deferred-revenue business. Horizon is 10 years because margins are still normalizing off the FY2023 trough and the 2030 capacity target implies growth continuing well past year 5. Terminal cap multiple held at 12x base (cyclical/commodity agribusiness, well below the 20x tech default) given inherent price-taker economics versus Californian supply.

bear.narrative: Bear case: SHV's FY2023-style downside repeats -- a sharp adverse move in the global almond price (Californian supply surprises upward, as almost happened intra-FY2025 on a surprise USDA crop estimate), compounded by a weak/wet crop year (NSW orchards, which the Analysis JSON notes remain in multi-year recovery, disappoint again) and margin pressure from uncontrollable input cost inflation (water, bees, fertiliser, energy -- H1 FY2026 alone absorbed ~$18m of this). China demand or trade-policy conditions turn against Australian exporters (60-65% customer concentration), removing the current tariff advantage. The CEO transition (David Surveyor's FY23-25 turnaround leadership departing for an unproven incoming CEO) coincides with execution missing on the capital-intensive 2030 targets, so incremental capex is spent without the associated margin/volume payoff. FY1 revenue contracts -3% (a bad crop + price pullback), EBITDA margin falls toward the FY2022/24 trough band (13-17%), lease cost is a heavier drag as a share of a smaller revenue base, and owner FCF is modestly negative in years 1-3 before recovering -- a real but survivable trough, not a going-concern scenario, given FY2025's deleveraged balance sheet (gearing 15.1%).

base.narrative: Base case: SHV settles into a normal mid-cycle year on an EBITDA basis (like FY2025's 19.2% Underlying EBITDA margin), but WITHOUT the one-off working-capital release that inflated FY2025's reported owner FCF -- so the true owner-FCF margin normalizes to ~4% once the lease cost (~8.5% of revenue, a large leased-orchard book) and PP&E D&A/capex are deducted. Revenue grows from volume/mix (external grower tonnes toward the 20,000MT+ target, value-added Allinga Farms product growth, modest own-crop recovery) at 6% tapering to 3% over 10 years -- well short of management's 2030 target of $700m/65,000MT, treated as aspirational rather than a base-case anchor. Cash tax ramps from FY2025's near-zero rate (carried-forward losses) to the 30% AU statutory rate by year 5, per the company's own disclosure that it expects to generate taxable income from 2026 onward.

bull.narrative: Bull case: the structural supply tailwind materializes as management describes it -- Californian bearing acreage keeps declining (first time since 1995), global almond prices stay structurally firmer, and demand grows at the top of the cited 5-7% CAGR range (China/India/Turkiye). SHV executes the 2030 plan close to plan: external grower volumes exceed 20,000MT, the value-added mix keeps growing (Allinga Farms paste +20%+), the in-line kernel recovery process lifts yields, and Australia's tariff advantage over the US into China persists or widens. EBITDA margin expands toward 23.5% as processing scale (50,000MT->65,000MT) and cost-saving programs (the $10m two-year target) land, and lease cost falls as a share of revenue as the book amortises while revenue outgrows it. New CEO transition is a non-event. Revenue reaches ~$800m by year 10, near management's $700m 2030 target.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the 15% house default to 30%: this is a global-commodity price-taker (no pricing power against Californian supply, ~75-80% of world volume) with high customer concentration (China ~60-65% of exports), a demonstrated capacity for near-loss years within the last three (FY2023 NPAT -$114.7m), and a CEO transition landing squarely on top of the most capital-intensive growth plan in the company's history (2030 targets). Bull weight trimmed to 25% because the bull case requires several independent things to go right simultaneously (acreage-decline thesis, execution on 65,000MT/$700m targets, margin expansion to 23.5%, continued China demand/tariff advantage) with a new, unproven CEO. Base gets the remaining 45%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
